reason: Weight is carried by three restrictive clusters, all labeled toward agreeing: the two Basic Law immigration bills (rows 1-2, ~46% of weight) limiting entry, stay and status of non-citizens including asylum seekers; the bills exempting employers of foreign caregivers from pension contributions (rows 3-5, 12, 17, ~27%) cutting a foreign worker benefit; and the infiltrator money-transfer, unspent-deposit and driving-licence bans (rows 6-9, 23, 30, ~14%). The light 'away' bills (caregiver visa extensions, access to courts) are the mirror image of the same question. The statement 'make it harder to stay, work or receive benefits, even if their living conditions worsen' covers stay (Basic Laws), work and benefits (pension, deposits, licence) as one restrictive stance and names the price; agree = less matches the toward labels. Off-topic light bills: labour laws applied to workers in Judea and Samaria (Palestinian/settlement employment, not foreign workers), election-day pay/day off, and the exam exemption for foreign-trained nurses; together about 8 weight points, negligible.
